title: F7 — the water surface, round 6. The round was sent at a multiplier the decomposition said cost 30.67 presence points. It ran the two halves of that term's gate apart for the first time in four rounds, found the gate is worth 4 points and the multiplier is worth 40, and derived the bound that says no value of either can clear the acceptance while a fade still exists. It also ran the `|span|` drift measurement ARBITRATION S67 says nobody had done, and found the control every water_edge run in this piece has banked since round 2 and no round ever measured.
verdict_this_answers: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-F7-WATER-r5.json (FAIL at 2/10, held not lowered). Its round-6 instruction: retire and replace the width gate before dispatching anything; target the alpha multiplier and do NOT promise it clears the acceptance; attack TemporalVar and hf_survival together.
what_i_could_not_do: **THE ACCEPTANCE STILL FAILS AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT, AND THE MOST USEFUL THING I HAVE IS THE REASON IT CANNOT BE CLEARED BY TUNING.** At deep-marshes `edge-b135`, threshold 16, in ONE interleaved run with a 3.83-point drift band, the shore alpha term's multiplier maps to presence as: **.00 -> 22.44% | .42 -> 50.77% (the shipped r5 arm) | .70 -> 72.78% (what I ship) | no term at all -> 91.18%**. That is ~63 presence points per unit of multiplier across four measured values, nearly linear. Interpolating between the measured .70 and the measured no-fade point, **presence reaches the 90% bar at a multiplier of about 0.98 — an alpha reduction of two per cent, which is not a fade.** So at this pose the 90% presence clause and a visible shore fade are mutually exclusive under this mechanism. **A seventh round that tunes either the band or the multiplier cannot clear the acceptance, and I would rather say that than ship a number that looks like progress.**

**AND THE TARGET I WAS SENT AT IS NOT WHERE THE COST LIVES. MY OWN ARM FALSIFIED MY OWN BRIEF'S READING.** The r5 decomposition (91.34 / 60.67 / 51.38) was read as *round 3's transmittance gate costs 30.67 points, go and remove it*. Nobody had ever run the two halves of `esShoreT = 1-(1-esTrans)*(1-esBandM)` apart — four rounds moved only the band. Run apart, at the same pose, in one run: **union .42 -> 50.77%, band-gate-only .42 -> 54.42%, transmittance-gate-only .42 -> 60.66%, no fade -> 91.18%.** Removing EITHER gate recovers 4 to 10 points of the ~40 the term costs; **the metre band alone reproduces 36.8 of the union's 40.4 points.** The gates are strongly sub-additive and neither is the term. **The 30.67 figure is correct arithmetic and a misleading target, and it travelled from a verdict into a brief into this build before an arm was pointed at it.**

**I HAVE NO MEASURE OF THE THING THIS ITEM IS BUILDING, AND SIX ROUNDS HAVE NOT HAD ONE.** Both admissible measures — `presence` and the new `shore_contrast_retained_pct` — are **monotone increasing in the shore fade's multiplier at the deep-marshes pose**, so at that pose both are maximised by having no fade at all. A shoreline depth fade exists to remove `RI-VIS04` §9's TELL, *a hard geometric line where the water plane intersects the terrain*. **Nothing in this piece measures that line.** Every instrument F7 has built measures what the fade COSTS. That is why the round ships a constant it can defend on two damage measures and cannot defend as a shoreline. It is a `blind_pair` question and `CLAUDE.md` rule 0e puts it with the orchestrator. `blind_status: not_possible`, 0, fails closed, for the sixth round running.

**MY OWN NEW CLAUSE IS NOT AS GOOD AS THE ONE IT SITS BESIDE, AND I SAY SO IN THE ITEM.** `RI-VIS03` M12b's `shore_contrast_retained_pct` is threshold-CONDITIONAL on arms: one arm reads **40.98 / 33.84 / 28.43%** at thresholds 6 / 10 / 16, a 12.6-point spread against a 0.72-point drift band. `presence` on the identical captures reads **50.49 / 50.63 / 50.77** — a 0.28-point spread. **So the clause I wrote is an order of magnitude less threshold-portable than the measure that already existed**, it does not displace it, and a number under it may never be carried between thresholds. Written into the item itself, not just here.

**THE WESTERN ROOTLANDS FALSIFIED THE FIRST DRAFT OF MY OWN CLAUSE, WITHIN THE ROUND.** I wrote that the contrast measure is *maximised by deleting the shore fade*, from four deep-marshes poses. At western-rootlands `edge-b045` it is not: **`no-shorefade` retains 100.27% and both FADING arms retain 105.7%** — the fade RAISES the water's shoreline contrast there, on a 0.056-level baseline drift. So the direction of the measure depends on the pose and my generalisation was a pattern I wanted from one region. Corrected in `RI-VIS03` M12b the same turn. **This is `ARBITRATION` S66's exact shape and I filed it against myself.**

**I RAN BROWSERS WHILE `node tools/contention.mjs` REPORTED THE BOX OVER ITS CEILING, AND THE TOOL ASKS THAT THIS BE SAID.** Every reading taken this round, in order: **2.08 GO, 1.58 GO, 4.33 WAIT, 4.22 WAIT, 3.28 GO, 4.03 WAIT, 3.94 GO** per core against a 4.0 ceiling. I launched only on a GO; the WAIT readings occurred with runs already in flight. When the box went over I launched nothing further and killed no running measurement (HAZARDS §23, §13). The visible cost is that the western-rootlands run is slow enough that it will not finish all four bearings inside its timeout.

**THE WESTERN ROOTLANDS IS STILL SHORT OF `RI-VIS03` M12a CLAUSE 1, FOR THE THIRD ROUND RUNNING, AND THIS TIME IT IS TRUNCATION RATHER THAN A CHOICE.** I dispatched all four declared bearings. What completed is recorded in `job_5`; the run banks `sweep.json` after every arm so whatever landed is real, and whatever did not is absent rather than approximated. **M12a clause 1 fails closed there again.**

**I DID NOT RE-SHOOT `TemporalVar` AND IT REMAINS THE HARD FAIL THE r5 CRITIC MEASURED — ON THE WRONG ARM.** The r5 critic confirmed 0.000341 against a >= 0.002 band and a 0.0005 hard-fail floor, and named its own limit: the sequence was shot on the arm called `fixed` at a commit where `fixed` was still 1.20 m, so **it has never been measured on any shipped arm.** `--mode motion` in `tools/visual/f7-r6-sweep.mjs` carries the r5 write-ordering fix and would bank it properly. I did not spend the browser on it, because the box went to WAIT and the gate question and the preservation set were worth more. **So M12's `TemporalVar` row for the r6 build does not exist. Not 'passes', not 'fails' — does not exist**, and a critic must not read the r5 number as this build's.

**I DID NOT ABLATE THE RIPPLE COEFFICIENTS, WHICH THE r5 VERDICT NAMED AS ITS THIRD ROUND-6 ITEM.** `TemporalVar` and `hf_survival` may be one defect at the three procedural terms. Untouched, untested, and `ARBITRATION` S63 forbids me narrating it. The one thing I did do is repair the CITATION that points at them: `RI-VIS11` §2 said *lines 304-306* and the terms were at 323-325 — and round 6 edits that region again, so I replaced the line number with the grep that finds the symbols. **A line number is a citation with a half-life.**

**THE GATE CHANGE COSTS A REVERSIBILITY PROPERTY ROUND 4 BUILT ON PURPOSE, AND I AM NOT HIDING IT.** With the union in place, `uWaterShoreBandM -> 1e-4` restored round 3 EXACTLY from a uniform, with no shader edit. With `esShoreT = esBandM` it restores NOTHING — the fade vanishes entirely, which is the `no-shorefade` arm, not the `r3` arm. **Round 3's gate is no longer reachable without a shader edit** (`transonly` in `tools/visual/f7-r6-sweep.mjs`). What a critic keeps: `uWaterShoreFade = 0` still ablates the whole line, and the band still sweeps.

**NO FRAME-TIME READING, AND I DID NOT ATTEMPT ONE.** Round 4 established by measurement that it is unobtainable on this SwiftShader box (3703.09 ms/world-pass, replicate spread 5605.27) and `game/src/engine.js` puts `renderCpuMs` in `_unmeasurable` in its own words. Inherited, not re-derived, and marked as such.

**I DID NOT RE-DERIVE THE OFFLINE BAND CENSUS (59.81% / 3.11%, 100% / 17.98%) — AND ROUND 6 GIVES A REASON TO DOUBT IT AS A PREDICTOR.** That census counts WET CORNERS on a 12.5 m lattice whose band coverage at 0.10 m it puts at 3.11% in the Deep Marshes. Measured on screen at `edge-b135`, the band gate ALONE removes 36.8 presence points. **A per-corner census cannot see how much SCREEN a 0.10 m band covers at a grazing view**, and the two instruments should not be read as saying the same thing. I did not re-run the census; I am flagging the inference, not the number.

job_2_the_span_drift_run_S67_said_nobody.why_it_matters: `ARBITRATION` S67 retired `gradient_width_px >= 12` because the measure is exactly invariant under any rescaling of the luma profile. Its named replacement was a contrast clause on `|span|`, and the r5 critic refused to land it under `CRITIC-DOCTRINE` §1.3's third guard because **`|span|` had never had a drift measurement**. That restraint was right and the run was cheap.
job_2_the_span_drift_run_S67_said_nobody.and_it_needed_no_browser: `f7-r5-sweep.mjs --interleave` re-captures the UNCHANGED baseline arm before and after every arm and runs `shoreProfile()` on every one of them. So `poses[].baseline_captures[].by_threshold[].shore.span` is a repeated measurement of one unchanged shader across exactly the ordinals the arms occupy — `HAZARDS` §25a rule 3's definition of the right noise floor. **33 such captures were already on disk across 6 runs, 4 poses, 2 regions, 5 commits and 2 processes.** Tool: `tools/visual/f7-r6-offline.mjs --mode span` and `--mode spanctl`.
job_2_the_span_drift_run_S67_said_nobody.THE_CONTROL_NOBODY_HAD_EVER_MEASURED: A bare `span` is inadmissible for the same reason a bare `NormalEnergy` is: it is a property of a region of screen as much as of a shader. The bank casts shade, a shoreline strip mesh sits on the boundary, and the distance bins nearest land carry both. **Every `water_edge` run in this piece has banked the control since round 2 and no round ever ran a profile over it** — the `--water-hidden` frame is the identical pixels with all water meshes removed. Its own span at deep-marshes `edge-b135` is **-14.689**, i.e. bed and bank alone carry a LARGER near-shore/open-water gradient than the water does, with the opposite sign. Every span number published before this round counted that as the water's.
job_2_the_span_drift_run_S67_said_nobody.the_measure: `span_water_minus_hidden = span(arm) - span(water-hidden)`, and because that is threshold-dependent in absolute levels, the reportable quantity is `shore_contrast_retained_pct = 100 x span_water_minus_hidden(arm) / span_water_minus_hidden(unchanged baseline arm)`.

job_3_the_finding_i_did_not_go_looking_f.headline: **THE 'DRIFT BAND' THIS PIECE HAS PUBLISHED FOR TWO ROUNDS IS NOT NOISE. THE CAPTURE PIPELINE IS BYTE-DETERMINISTIC, AND THE SPREAD ACROSS ORDINALS IS A REPRODUCIBLE SETTLING TRANSIENT.**
job_3_the_finding_i_did_not_go_looking_f.how_i_found_it: Checking whether `dm-b135-null` and `dm-b135-verify` were two independent processes — the r5 critic reported they reproduce to three decimals, and my span tool printed their baseline drift as identical to the digit, which is not what three decimals of agreement looks like.
job_3_the_finding_i_did_not_go_looking_f.the_measurement: `md5sum` over baseline frames from separate processes at separate commits: `dm-b225-sweep/edge-b225--BASE-o0.png` and `dm-b225-reverse/edge-b225--BASE-o0.png` are **byte-identical**; so are their `BASE-o2` and `BASE-o4`; so are the two `edge-b135` runs' `BASE-o0`. The same arm at a DIFFERENT ordinal is not (`r3-o1` vs `r3-o5` differ).
job_3_the_finding_i_did_not_go_looking_f.what_it_changes: The interleaved-flanking correction the r5 tool applies is the RIGHT remedy, and more strongly than its author argued: it is removing a deterministic trend, not averaging noise. But the published band is a **bias bound, not a standard deviation**, replication cannot shrink it, and calling it a noise floor — which round 5, the r5 critic and this brief all do — is wrong. It is still the right number to print beside every result.
job_3_the_finding_i_did_not_go_looking_f.what_it_does_not_change: Nothing in the r5 verdict's conclusions depends on the band being stochastic. Every effect this round reports is 10x to 90x the band either way.
job_3_the_finding_i_did_not_go_looking_f.the_limit_of_the_finding: Byte-identity held across two commits INSIDE round 5's commit range. It did NOT hold between round 5 and round 6 — my `edge-b135` BASE-o0 and water-hidden frames differ from round 5's, and the hidden-frame masked luma moved 1.56 levels, because other pieces changed the world between them. **Determinism is per-world, not absolute**, which is `HAZARDS` §12's family.
